Evaluating observed weather in Auckland

This report summarises data from personal observations of the weather in Auckland.
The observations include time of day, whether it was raining, how cloudy the sky was, and an estimated temperature (Celsius).

Do clouds mean rain?

My main thought while collecting this data was how strong the correlation between cloudiness and rain would be, so let’s have a look!

Plot 1

As we can see above, the data generally align with expectations: no rain on clear observations, just under a third of partly cloudy observations had rain, and overcast observations had nearly 70% rain!

How did the temperature change?

Seeing as the cloudiness and rainfall data went as expected, how about we look at how the temperature changed over time?

Plot 2

As expected of the time of year this data was collected, we see a steady decrease in the temperature the further from summer and closer to winter the data gets.

How about at the different times of day?

Let’s take a closer look at when the temperature data was collected during the day.

Plot 3

Here we see that the temperatures for each time of day go from lower to middle of the pack in the morning, to higher in the afternoon (including the peak temperatures), then middle for the afternoon, before finally getting lower at night.
